intro: MIDI to WAV turns MIDI files into uncompressed WAV audio, the format audio and video editors, music workstations and mastering software need. It is the way to bring a MIDI piece into Audacity, Reaper, Premiere, DaVinci Resolve or a mixing desk without losing quality.

The sound is generated by FluidSynth with the FluidR3_GM bank, which holds the 128 General MIDI instruments and drums, sampled from real instruments. Tempo and its changes, each channel's programs, volume, panning, pedals and reverb are honoured.

The WAV is stereo, 16-bit PCM, at 44.1 kHz (CD quality) or 48 kHz (the video standard). We work out the MIDI's duration before synthesising and apply your plan's audio minute limit, so you know in advance whether it fits.

Drum tracks on MIDI channel 10 use the General MIDI drum kit, and pitch bends, modulation and sustain pedal are rendered as in a hardware synthesiser. The result is a finished stereo mix you can drop straight into a project, with no need to install a synthesiser or a sound bank on your computer.
Synthesis runs on our server, with the synthesiser as a separate program and limited time and memory. You can convert up to 20 files at once and download them in a ZIP.
steps: Upload one or more MIDI files.
Download the WAV or the ZIP.

faq.a: 44.1 kHz for music and CD; 48 kHz if the audio goes into a video, because that is what video editors use.
About 10 MB per minute, because WAV does not compress. If you only want to listen to it, MIDI to MP3 is ten times smaller.

faq.q: Can I get each instrument on its own track?
faq.a: No: a stereo mix with everything is produced. Separate tracks need a sequencer.
